We're getting ready to wire the August invoice (attached) and want to confirm the best path to avoid shortfalls on receipt. A few questions:

- We can either send an EUR wire to the EU virtual IBAN you provided previously, or send USD via SWIFT. Which do you recommend for lower fees/clean reconciliation?
- If we send via our bank's SWIFT chain, intermediary (correspondent) banks typically deduct fees en route. Will Redwood accept the net amount (i.e., beneficiary receives amount minus mid-rail fees) or do you require us to send OUR so the payer covers all intermediary fees?
- For VAT purposes: can you confirm you will issue an EU VAT invoice when we pay from our EU entity, and that the invoice number/PO should appear in the remittance?
- Finally, please send any specific remittance CSV format you want (columns). We do batch payments and want our AP system to map correctly.

Carlos — thanks for the note and the invoice attachment. Short answers up-front: we can accept both EUR virtual IBAN and USD SWIFT; to guarantee full settlement we strongly prefer the payer selects OUR (payer covers ALL fees). Below is more detail and the practical trade-offs.

Option A — EUR (Virtual IBAN / sweep):
- If you can originate a SEPA or a EUR wire into the virtual IBAN we provided, that will generally avoid correspondent chain fees and is the cleanest option for reconciliation.
- Virtual IBAN -> our sweep consolidates into the regional pool; you should see the full invoice amount on our side (no mid-rail deductions).
- Recommended when both parties operate in EUR.

Option B — USD SWIFT (your bank -> correspondent chain -> beneficiary):
- If you go SWIFT, intermediary/correspondent banks may deduct a fee.
- Our policy: unless instructed otherwise, we credit the amount we actually receive (i.e., net). If you need Redwood to be credited with the gross invoice total, please arrange payment with charges=OUR.
- If charges=SHA (shared), the receiving side may still be short by intermediary fees that neither side explicitly covers.

VAT/invoice handling:
- If payment is originating from your EU-registered entity and you provide the EU VAT ID on the PO/payment, we will issue an EU VAT invoice. For US/ROW entities, VAT is not applied.

Practical recommendation:
1) Use the virtual IBAN if possible (minimal friction).
2) If SWIFT is necessary, set charges=OUR.
3) Include the invoice number, PO, and our HubSpot deal id (DL-2027-1183) in the remittance reference to speed reconciliation.

Attached is a short wire template (redwood_wire_template_v2.csv) showing required fields (beneficiary name, IBAN, BIC/SWIFT, reference). Laura — looping you for billing reconciliation rules and VAT specifics.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Carlos — quick clarifications from billing: 

- CSV remittance: your column set is good. Our preferred header order: invoice_number, PO_number, invoice_date, gross_amount, tax_amount, currency, beneficiary_account, internal_reference, hubspot_deal_id. I attached a one-row sample (remittance_sample.csv).

- VAT: confirmed — if payment originates from your DE entity and you provide the VAT ID we will issue an invoice with VAT line and your VAT ID listed. We will need the exact legal entity name to match the VAT invoice.

- Incidental intermediary fees: we can't broadly absorb correspondent bank fees as a policy. However, for pilots we can accept a one-time concession up to $5 per wire for a short window (3 payments) — this requires approval and an audit trail. If you'd like that concession, we'll record a billing credit afterward. Otherwise please set charges=OUR or add a small buffer (recommended).

- For reconciliation: please send the first payment's bank statement (or a SWIFT MT103) so our AR team can reconcile the exact credits and apply them to invoice-7789. After that we can automate match rules.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the legal entity name and VAT ID to appear on the invoice.
2) Confirm whether you will use the EUR virtual IBAN or SWIFT+OUR (and whether you want the pilot concession).
3) Send remittance CSV and, once wired, a payment confirmation (MT103 or bank statement extract).

Thanks — I'll prepare any billing credit paperwork if you opt into the pilot concession.

Laura Bennett
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
